rules.statement: Use SHA-256 as the Concat KDF digest for ECDH-ES key agreement (ECDH-ES, ECDH-ES+A128KW/A192KW/A256KW) no matter which curve is used; never pick the digest from the curve or key size.
rules.why: RFC 7518 §4.6.2 says the digest method is SHA-256. A digest that depends on the curve produces keys on P-384/P-521 that no conforming JOSE implementation can reproduce, and the failure is silent.
rules.check: Look for ECDH-ES key derivation code that picks SHA-384/SHA-512 from the curve, key size or crv value, or that passes the curve size into the KDF or its reps computation.

rules.statement: Don't use Windows CNG NCryptDeriveKey with SP800_56A_CONCAT and no explicit KDF hash algorithm for JWE ECDH-ES key derivation; use the managed, RFC-conforming derivation.
rules.why: The CNG path derives a key on P-384 and P-521 that does not conform to RFC 7518.
rules.check: Look for CngKey or NCryptDeriveKey-based ECDH derivation in JOSE code or tests, especially without an explicit hash.

rules.statement: When a test checks cryptographic output against a third-party implementation, use an oracle known to conform to the specification (prefer the spec's own test vectors), and when a library offers both a platform-native and a managed path, use the managed, conforming path.
rules.why: Two implementations agreeing only proves something if one is known to conform. A non-conforming oracle hid a defect behind a green test suite.
rules.check: Look for cross-check tests whose oracle is a platform-native crypto path (for example CNG or jose-jwt EcdhKeyManagementWin with CngKey), or that rely only on another implementation's output when spec test vectors exist.

rules.statement: Don't let a conformance test's expected value depend on the host platform; the same assertions must hold on every OS.
rules.why: A test whose expected value changes with the platform can't express a conformance requirement, and it keeps asserting known-broken behavior on some platforms.
rules.check: Look for OperatingSystem.IsWindows() or similar branches that pick different expected crypto results or different oracles, and for assertions limited to a subset of inputs (for example P-256 only) to avoid known failures.

rules.statement: Target portable TFMs (for example net10.0) in projects, including test projects, rather than platform-specific TFMs such as net10.0-windows chosen just to reach platform-native cryptographic types.
rules.why: A platform-specific TFM stops the solution from building on Linux CI and tends to bring the platform's non-conforming behavior into the assertions.
rules.check: Look in .csproj diffs for TargetFramework(s) values with an OS suffix such as -windows.
